title: Siemens CTO update on Calibre at DAC 2026
gist: Siemens EDA CTO Juan Rey discusses Calibre's evolution at DAC 2026: new 3DThermal and 3DStress products for 2.5D/3D packaging, embedded AI/ML for faster debug and setup, AI agents in IC design, and EDA models as digital twins. The piece is a favorable interview.

insights.claim: Calibre's differentiation, per Siemens EDA's CTO, is engineering focus on quality and reliable results, with performance, short run times and scalability under a small memory footprint.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Physical verification sign-off is sticky; this is the vendor's own framing and promotional in tone.

insights.claim: Siemens EDA has early access to leading IC design customers, which it says lets it introduce new products for emerging verification challenges.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Customer co-development supports Siemens' position as nodes and packaging evolve.
insights.locator: Siemens EDA has the benefit of early access

insights.claim: Advanced packaging with 2.5D and 3D chiplet stacking creates new physical verification needs such as thermal, stress and reliability analysis, beyond progress from FinFET to GAA, nanosheet and CFET.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Packaging complexity expands the EDA verification TAM.

insights.claim: Calibre 3DThermal runs thermal analysis throughout the 3D IC flow and analyzes cross-die coupling, thermal and stress impacts from the user-defined stack-up.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Product evidence of Siemens' 3D IC portfolio build-out.

insights.claim: Calibre 3DStress lets teams manage thermal-mechanical stress during and after packaging, to identify and mitigate warpage, cracking and mobility changes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Warpage and cracking are yield risks in advanced packaging; tools addressing them have a clear value case.

insights.claim: AI and ML inside Calibre can triage runs reporting millions of errors into common groups and prioritize which to fix first, and improve setup times by allocating CPU and GPU resources efficiently.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: AI gains in EDA are productivity-led and tied to GPU-aware compute, not replacing sign-off engines.
insights.locator: AI and ML technologies have been added

insights.claim: AI agents in IC design are used to find the source of errors, suggest fixes and verify them, and future designs improve from learned experience of previous designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Agentic EDA flows could shorten design cycles; maturity is not evidenced in the article.

insights.claim: Siemens frames EDA models as digital twins that must be dynamic, changeable and always in sync with the design specification, spanning chips, boards, data-center racks and thermal reliability across workloads.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Connects EDA to Siemens' broader digital-twin strategy and to data-center-scale system design.
insights.locator: Siemens has been providing the vision for using Digital Twins
